meaning: the entity is one Map Creator export's own table of contents: which of the nineteen files the site shipped, which of them were empty and in which form, the per-file headers that are envelopes rather than model data, and how each file's text was written beyond its values

schema.$comment: Open to fields a newer producer adds (SPEC §9). Derived from `records.rs`'s field map by `vocabulary()`; edit the map, not this.
schema.description: the entity is one Map Creator export's own table of contents: which of the nineteen files the site shipped, which of them were empty and in which form, the per-file headers that are envelopes rather than model data, and how each file's text was written beyond its values

conveyor_header.description: `conveyor.json`'s own dialect version and its vendor port classification, which sit beside the conveyor list rather than in it.

files.description: Each file the site shipped, and the form it arrived in: `array`, `object`, `empty_array` or `empty_object`. A file the site never shipped is absent from this map. All four are different facts — five of the nineteen files are empty on every site seen, three of them as `{}` and the rest as `[]` — and the export reproduces whichever it found rather than guessing.

key_order.description: The order the file wrote the keys of an object of this record in, for each object whose order is not the one the export entity's `key_orders` gives an object with the same keys at the same place, by its JSON pointer from the record's own object (`""` for that object; on the export entity, which holds what lies outside every record, the file's name and its pointer in the file). JSON gives key order no meaning; the export writes each file back byte for byte, so the order is a fact this document carries.

key_orders.description: How the export's files usually order an object's keys: for each place an object stands at in a file, with list positions left out (`map.json[].map_values[]` is every cell), and for each set of keys an object there states, the order most objects with that set state it in when the set first appears, which a later import keeps while any object there still states the set; the orders kept first, then the sets most objects state. A record whose object departs records its own order (`key_order`); for an object no file stated, the place's first order serves.

location_profiles_empty.description: `true` when `map.json` states `location_profiles` as an empty list, which no profile entity can say: a floor object stating no list and one stating an empty list are two texts. Absent otherwise.

pps_bin_envelope.description: The captured HTTP request `pps_bin.json` is stored as — url, method and headers. Not model data, and carried because the export has to write the file back as it found it.

pptl_empty_groups.description: The places in `pptl.json`, counting from zero, of the groups that hold no device. A group is rebuilt from its devices, so one with none has nothing else to say it stood there.

spacing.description: How each file's text lays its value out, where it is not one compact line with nothing around it: `separators`, the one between two items and the one between a key and its value; `indent`, the unit each line is indented by per level, where every item stands on a line of its own; `before` and `after`, the whitespace around the value. A file whose text no such spacing writes is refused at ingest, naming what in it cannot be written back.

written_negative_zero.description: The JSON pointers, from the record's own object (on the export entity, the file's name and the pointer in the file), of the zeros the file wrote with a minus sign (`-0.0`), which a reader holds as the zero without one, so that the export writes them back with one.

written_with_point.description: The JSON pointers, from the record's own object (on the export entity, the file's name and the pointer in the file), of the whole numbers the file wrote with a decimal point (`40.0`), which a reader spells as integers, so that the export writes them back with one.

schema.title: mapcreator.export
